Note: 54-year-old male with 35 pack-year smoking history presents with 3 months of persistent cough and intermittent wheezing. Reports mild hemoptysis twice in the past week and 8 lb unintentional weight loss over 4 months. Denies fever or recent travel. Past history significant for COPD managed intermittently with albuterol. Vitals today: T 37.2°C, HR 92, BP 138/84, RR 18, SpO₂ 94% on room air. Chest exam reveals scattered wheezes and diminished breath sounds in right upper field. CBC shows mild normocytic anemia (Hgb 11.8). CXR demonstrates right upper lobe opacity described as possible consolidation versus mass; radiologist suggests correlation with CT. Started on azithromycin for presumed atypical pneumonia and prednisone taper for possible COPD exacerbation. CT chest ordered. Advised smoking cessation. Follow-up in 2 weeks or sooner if hemoptysis worsens.

62-year-old female presents with progressive fatigue and intermittent abdominal discomfort for 6 months. Reports change in bowel habits with alternating constipation and loose stools, attributes to diet. Notes dark stools on occasion but takes iron supplements. Vitals stable; BP 126/70, HR 88. BMI 27. Labs reveal iron deficiency anemia (Hgb 9.6, ferritin 8). CMP within normal limits. FOBT positive. No prior colonoscopy. Abdomen soft with mild left lower quadrant tenderness. Differential includes chronic GI blood loss vs inflammatory bowel disease. Started oral iron therapy, referred for colonoscopy and GI evaluation. Advised to monitor for overt bleeding or worsening pain. Follow-up after endoscopic evaluation.

45-year-old premenopausal woman with 4 months of increasingly heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pressure. Reports urinary frequency and bloating. No significant weight change. Exam reveals enlarged, irregularly contoured uterus palpable above symphysis. Vitals normal. Hgb 10.5. Pelvic ultrasound shows 8 cm heterogeneous uterine mass, possibly fibroid though atypical features noted. Endometrial stripe 7 mm. Prescribed tranexamic acid for bleeding and NSAIDs for pain. MRI pelvis ordered for better characterization. Discussed possibility of benign leiomyoma versus other uterine pathology. Follow-up in 3 weeks with imaging results.

28-year-old male presents with 2 months of night sweats, fatigue, and painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Denies recent infections but reports pruritus after hot showers. Vitals: T 37.8°C, HR 96. Exam shows multiple rubbery, non-tender lymph nodes in left neck and supraclavicular region. CBC shows mild leukocytosis (WBC 13.2) with eosinophilia. ESR elevated at 55. Chest X-ray reveals widened mediastinum versus technical artifact. Started on symptomatic antihistamines for itching. Referred for excisional lymph node biopsy and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. Follow-up pending pathology.

39-year-old female notes palpable left breast lump for 1 month, mildly tender, fluctuates slightly with cycle. No nipple discharge. Family history of breast disease in aunt. Vitals normal. Clinical exam reveals 2 cm firm, mobile mass in upper outer quadrant without skin changes. No axillary lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic mammogram shows dense breast tissue with indeterminate lesion; ultrasound suggests complex cyst versus solid mass. Prescribed short course of NSAIDs and advised caffeine reduction. Referred for core needle biopsy. Follow-up scheduled after pathology results.

60-year-old male with progressive headaches over 3 months, worse in mornings, occasionally associated with nausea. Wife reports subtle personality changes and forgetfulness. No focal weakness reported. Vitals stable. Neuro exam reveals mild right pronator drift. Fundoscopy equivocal for papilledema. MRI brain ordered after CT showed left frontal hypodense area possibly representing subacute infarct versus mass lesion. Started on dexamethasone for cerebral edema and levetiracetam for seizure prophylaxis given brief episode of confusion last week. Neurology referral urgent. Close follow-up within one week.

52-year-old fair-skinned woman presents with enlarging pigmented lesion on upper back, noticed 6 months ago. Occasional bleeding after scratching. No systemic symptoms. Vitals normal. Skin exam shows 1.3 cm asymmetric lesion with irregular borders and color variegation. Dermoscopy inconclusive. No palpable regional lymph nodes. Excisional biopsy planned. Advised strict sun protection. Follow-up for pathology review in 10 days.

67-year-old male with urinary hesitancy, weak stream, and nocturia x4 nightly for 1 year, recently worsening. Mild lower back discomfort. No hematuria. Digital rectal exam reveals enlarged, firm prostate with asymmetry. PSA 6.8 ng/mL (previous 3.9 one year ago). Urinalysis negative for infection. Started on tamsulosin. Referred to urology for further evaluation including possible prostate biopsy. Advised to report urinary retention or worsening pain.

48-year-old female with neck fullness and mild dysphagia to solids. Reports heat intolerance and 5 lb weight loss despite normal appetite. Vitals: HR 102, BP 130/76. Exam reveals palpable 3 cm right thyroid nodule. TSH suppressed at 0.1, free T4 mildly elevated. Thyroid ultrasound shows solitary hypoechoic nodule with microcalcifications. Started on propranolol for symptom control. Referred for fine needle aspiration. Follow-up in 2 weeks with endocrinology.

72-year-old female with chronic right hip pain worsening over 5 months, now present at night. No trauma. History of osteoarthritis. Reports 10 lb weight loss unintentionally. Vitals stable. Exam reveals tenderness over proximal femur and limited range of motion. X-ray shows lytic-appearing lesion in proximal femur versus severe degenerative cyst. ESR mildly elevated. MRI ordered. Prescribed acetaminophen and advised partial weight-bearing with cane. Follow-up after imaging.

55-year-old male with persistent hoarseness for 4 months. History of GERD and tobacco use. Denies dysphagia but reports mild throat discomfort. Vitals normal. Laryngoscopy shows erythematous lesion on left vocal cord; unclear if inflammatory polyp versus neoplasm. Started on proton pump inhibitor and advised voice rest. Referred to ENT for biopsy. Follow-up in 3 weeks.

63-year-old female presents with vague epigastric pain radiating to back and new-onset painless jaundice noticed by family. Reports dark urine and pale stools. No fever. Vitals: BP 118/72, HR 90. Exam notable for scleral icterus and mild epigastric tenderness. Labs show total bilirubin 5.2, elevated ALP and GGT. Abdominal ultrasound reveals dilated common bile duct without visible stones. CT abdomen ordered for further evaluation. Prescribed cholestyramine for pruritus. Urgent GI referral arranged.

50-year-old male with intermittent gross hematuria over 2 weeks, no dysuria. Mild flank discomfort. No history of stones. Vitals stable. UA confirms RBCs, no infection. Creatinine 1.1. Renal ultrasound shows 3 cm left renal mass versus complex cyst. CT urogram scheduled. Advised hydration and avoidance of NSAIDs. Urology referral placed.

58-year-old postmenopausal woman with increasing abdominal girth, early satiety, and pelvic discomfort for 3 months. No vaginal bleeding. Vitals normal. Exam reveals shifting dullness suggestive of ascites and adnexal fullness on bimanual exam. CA-125 mildly elevated at 48. Transvaginal ultrasound shows complex cystic adnexal mass 6 cm. Referred to gynecologic oncology for evaluation. Symptomatic management with diuretics deferred pending specialist input. Follow-up within 1 week.

47-year-old male with intermittent rectal bleeding attributed to hemorrhoids, also reports change in stool caliber and fatigue. No significant weight loss. Vitals stable. Rectal exam shows internal hemorrhoids but also palpable irregularity higher in rectum. Hgb 10.9. Colonoscopy scheduled. Started stool softeners and topical hydrocortisone. Advised to monitor for increased bleeding or pain.

9-year-old female brought by parents for persistent low-grade fevers and fatigue for 6 weeks. Noted bruising on legs and decreased appetite. Vitals: T 38.1°C, HR 110. Exam reveals pallor and mild hepatosplenomegaly. CBC shows anemia (Hgb 8.7), thrombocytopenia (platelets 90k), and elevated WBC 18k with immature forms noted. Referred urgently to pediatric hematology for bone marrow evaluation. Supportive care instructions provided. Close follow-up arranged.

59-year-old male with history of chronic hepatitis presents with right upper quadrant discomfort and increasing abdominal swelling. Reports 12 lb weight loss. Vitals: BP 110/68, HR 95. Exam shows jaundice, ascites, and palpable firm liver edge. Labs reveal elevated AST/ALT, AFP elevated at 30. Ultrasound shows heterogeneous liver with focal lesion 4 cm. MRI liver ordered. Started on spironolactone for ascites and advised low-sodium diet. Hepatology referral placed.

70-year-old female with urinary urgency and microscopic hematuria on routine exam. No dysuria or fever. Past history significant for recurrent UTIs. Vitals stable. UA negative for nitrites/leukocyte esterase but persistent RBCs. Cystoscopy recommended. Started short empirical antibiotic course pending urine culture. Advised follow-up with urology.

25-year-old male athlete with persistent left knee pain for 3 months, worse at night, not relieved by rest. Initially treated as sports injury. Mild swelling noted. Vitals normal. X-ray shows periosteal reaction at distal femur. MRI ordered to evaluate for stress fracture versus other pathology. Prescribed NSAIDs cautiously and advised cessation of high-impact activity. Orthopedic referral made.

65-year-old female with early satiety, epigastric discomfort, and 15 lb weight loss over 5 months. Reports chronic NSAID use for arthritis. Occasional nausea, no vomiting. Vitals: BP 122/74, HR 88. Exam mild epigastric tenderness. Hgb 9.8 with microcytosis. Upper endoscopy scheduled to evaluate for peptic ulcer disease versus other gastric pathology. Started proton pump inhibitor and iron supplementation. Follow-up after endoscopy.

Mr. H is a 52-year-old male with a history of obesity and hypertension who presents for routine follow-up after reporting 3 months of polyuria, polydipsia, and 10-pound unintentional weight loss. Denies abdominal pain or blurred vision. BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 84 bpm, BMI 33.4 kg/m². Fasting glucose today 186 mg/dL, HbA1c 8.4%, urine microalbumin mildly elevated at 45 mg/g. Foot exam reveals intact sensation to monofilament, no ulcers. Initiated metformin 500 mg twice daily with plan to titrate as tolerated, continued lisinopril 20 mg daily, and started atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction. Counseled extensively on diet and exercise. Referral placed for diabetic education. Follow up in 3 months for repeat A1c and renal function testing.

Ms. R is a 24-year-old woman with childhood asthma presenting with 2 days of wheezing, chest tightness, and nocturnal cough after viral URI symptoms. Using rescue inhaler every 2 hours with partial relief. Vitals: T 37.2°C, HR 102 bpm, RR 22, O2 sat 94% on room air. Diffuse expiratory wheezes on exam. Peak flow 60% of personal best. Given nebulized albuterol in clinic with improvement to 75%. Prescribed prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days, refilled albuterol inhaler, and initiated fluticasone inhaler 110 mcg BID for better control. Reviewed inhaler technique. Advised to return or go to ED if worsening dyspnea. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

17-year-old male with no significant PMH presenting with 18 hours of periumbilical pain migrating to RLQ, associated with nausea and low-grade fever. Vitals: T 38.1°C, HR 110 bpm, BP 118/70. Abdomen tender at McBurney’s point with rebound. WBC 14.8 x10⁹/L with neutrophilia. CT abdomen confirms inflamed appendix without perforation. Started IV fluids, ceftriaxone and metronidazole, surgical consult obtained. Patient taken for laparoscopic appendectomy. Post-op plan includes pain management with acetaminophen/ibuprofen and outpatient surgical follow-up in 1 week.

Ms. L, 38-year-old teacher with past history of postpartum depression, reports 2 months of low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, and fatigue. Denies suicidal ideation. Vitals stable. PHQ-9 score 18. Labs including TSH and CBC within normal limits. Started sertraline 50 mg daily, advised on potential side effects. Referral to cognitive behavioral therapy placed. Encouraged regular exercise and sleep hygiene. Follow up in 4 weeks for medication assessment.

Mr. B is a 67-year-old with ischemic cardiomyopathy presenting with worsening lower extremity edema and dyspnea on exertion. Weight up 5 kg from baseline. BP 132/78, HR 88, O2 sat 95%. Bilateral crackles and 2+ pitting edema. BNP elevated at 780 pg/mL. Echocardiogram last month showed EF 35%. Increased furosemide to 40 mg BID, continued carvedilol and lisinopril. Reinforced sodium restriction and daily weights. Cardiology follow-up in 1 week and labs to monitor renal function.

45-year-old female smoker with productive cough, fever, and pleuritic chest pain for 3 days. T 38.5°C, HR 96, RR 20, O2 sat 92%. Crackles at right lower lobe. Chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. WBC 13.2. Started amoxicillin-clavulanate plus azithromycin. Advised hydration and smoking cessation counseling provided. Follow up in 48–72 hours if no improvement.

Ms. T, 50, presents with 6 months of bilateral hand stiffness lasting >1 hour in mornings, swelling at MCP and PIP joints. RF and anti-CCP positive. ESR 48 mm/hr. Started methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid supplementation. NSAIDs for symptomatic relief. Rheumatology referral arranged. Baseline liver function tests normal; will repeat labs in 4 weeks.

72-year-old male with longstanding diabetes and hypertension. Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73m². BP 150/88. Urinalysis with proteinuria. Adjusted lisinopril dose and reinforced glycemic control. Avoid NSAIDs. Referred to nephrology. Plan to monitor renal panel every 3 months.

29-year-old female with recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches associated with photophobia and nausea, occurring 3–4 times/month. Neuro exam normal. BP 118/72. Started sumatriptan PRN and initiated propranolol 40 mg BID for prophylaxis. Advised headache diary. Follow up in 6 weeks.

4-year-old boy with 2 days of ear pain and fever. T 38.3°C. Otoscopic exam shows bulging erythematous tympanic membrane on right. Prescribed amoxicillin 80 mg/kg/day divided BID. Acetaminophen for fever. Pediatric follow-up in 10 days.

35-year-old woman reports 2 months of intermittent joint pain in knees and wrists with fatigue, no clear swelling. Vitals stable. ANA pending, ESR mildly elevated. No rash or oral ulcers. Started trial of NSAIDs and ordered rheumatologic panel. Plan to reassess in 3 weeks once labs return.

46-year-old male with chronic heartburn worsened by late meals. BMI 29. Vitals normal. No alarm symptoms. Trial of omeprazole 20 mg daily initiated. Lifestyle counseling including weight loss and avoiding trigger foods. Follow up in 8 weeks.
60-year-old female with fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation. TSH 9.8 mIU/L, free T4 low. Started levothyroxine 50 mcg daily. Repeat TSH in 6 weeks.

68-year-old former smoker with chronic cough and dyspnea. FEV1 55% predicted on spirometry. O2 sat 93%. Initiated tiotropium inhaler daily and albuterol PRN. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines recommended. Pulmonary rehab referral placed.

34-year-old woman with heavy menses complaining of fatigue. Hb 9.6 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, ferritin low. Started oral ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID with vitamin C. Gynecology referral for menorrhagia evaluation. Recheck CBC in 2 months.
28-year-old male with well-demarcated plaques on elbows and scalp. No joint pain. Prescribed topical clobetasol and vitamin D analog. Dermatology follow-up in 6 weeks.
55-year-old woman with persistently elevated BP readings averaging 150/95. No end-organ damage symptoms. Started amlodipine 5 mg daily. Advised home BP monitoring and DASH diet. Follow up in 1 month.

40-year-old male with epigastric pain radiating to back after heavy alcohol intake. Lipase elevated at 650 U/L. CT consistent with mild pancreatitis. Admitted for IV fluids, pain control, NPO. Counseling on alcohol cessation. GI follow-up after discharge.
31-year-old female with excessive worry, muscle tension, insomnia for 6 months. GAD-7 score 16. Started escitalopram 10 mg daily and referred for psychotherapy. Follow up in 4 weeks.

22-year-old college athlete presenting after single syncopal episode during practice. No prior history. Vitals normal, ECG normal sinus rhythm. Basic labs unremarkable. Referred for Holter monitor and echocardiogram to rule out arrhythmia. Advised no strenuous activity until workup complete. Follow-up in cardiology clinic next week.

Patient: M.K., 67-year-old male. Former 40 pack-year smoker, quit approximately 8 years ago. Retired construction worker. PMH: COPD (on home O2 PRN), HTN, dyslipidemia. Presents today with a 3-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and a new productive cough. Wife noted he has lost approximately 18 lbs over the past 4 months without intentional dieting. On review of systems, patient endorses occasional hemoptysis over the past 6 weeks, right-sided shoulder and chest wall pain rated 5/10, and increasing fatigue. He initially attributed symptoms to worsening COPD.

On exam today: BP 138/84, HR 92, RR 20, SpO2 88% on room air (improved to 94% on 2L NC), Temp 37.1°C, Wt 71.2 kg (down from 79 kg documented 5 months ago). Breath sounds diminished in the right lower lobe with dullness to percussion. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy appreciated, though a small right supraclavicular node is palpable (~1.5 cm, firm). CXR obtained in office showed a right hilar mass with ipsilateral pleural effusion. CT chest with contrast ordered urgently, which returned showing a 4.7 x 3.8 cm right upper lobe spiculated mass with ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy and moderate pleural effusion. Labs: CBC with mild normocytic anemia (Hgb 10.2), LFTs WNL, BMP WNL, LDH elevated at 342 U/L. Calcium 10.8 (mildly elevated). PET-CT and brain MRI with contrast ordered. Interventional pulmonology referral placed for bronchoscopy with BAL and transbronchial biopsy. Thoracentesis also being coordinated through IP for pleural fluid cytology. Molecular and PD-L1 testing ordered on anticipated biopsy specimen. Spine imaging ordered given shoulder pain complaint to evaluate for osseous metastases.

Current meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg QHS, tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg daily, albuterol MDI PRN. Added today: dexamethasone 4 mg PO BID for symptom management pending staging workup, ondansetron 4 mg PO Q8H PRN nausea. Hydrocodone/acetaminophen 5/325 mg Q6H PRN for chest wall pain while awaiting further imaging.

Patient and family counseled that findings are highly concerning for malignancy, though tissue diagnosis is required before treatment planning. Multidisciplinary tumor board discussion planned once pathology and full staging are available. Follow-up scheduled in 10–14 days or sooner pending biopsy results. Smoking cessation resources reoffered; patient states he has not smoked since 2016.

Patient: D.L., 54-year-old female. No significant PMH. Never smoker, social alcohol use. Family history notable for father with colon cancer diagnosed at 62. She presents at the urging of her daughter after noticing increasingly dark stools over 2 months and one episode of frank rectal bleeding last week. She reports fatigue and some crampy lower abdominal pain, primarily on the left side. Denies fever or weight loss. Had a colonoscopy 7 years ago reported as normal. She was overdue for repeat screening.

BP 122/76, HR 88, RR 14, Temp 36.9°C, BMI 28.4. On abdominal exam, mild left lower quadrant tenderness without guarding or rebound. DRE: guaiac-positive stool, no palpable rectal mass. Labs: Hgb 9.8 g/dL with MCV 72 (microcytic anemia consistent with chronic blood loss), ferritin 7, serum iron low. CEA 14.3 ng/mL (elevated). BMP and LFTs normal. Urgent colonoscopy referral placed. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast obtained same day showing a 3.2 cm circumferential mass in the sigmoid colon with local mesenteric lymph node involvement and no obvious hepatic lesions. Colonoscopy performed 48 hours later confirming a fungating mass in the sigmoid colon; biopsies taken showing moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. MSI/MMR testing and KRAS/NRAS/BRAF molecular panel sent on biopsy specimen. MRI pelvis obtained to better characterize local extent.

Started ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO TID with vitamin C supplementation for iron deficiency anemia. Surgical oncology referral placed for sigmoid resection consideration; colorectal surgery clinic appointment confirmed for next week. Medical oncology referral placed. Patient counseled regarding potential need for neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy depending on surgical and pathologic staging. First-degree relatives advised to undergo colonoscopy given family history pattern.

Patient: R.T., 61-year-old male, right-handed, retired engineer. PMH: well-controlled T2DM, hypercholesterolemia. Brought in by his wife after a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds this morning. Wife reports that for the past 6 weeks he has had progressive word-finding difficulties, personality changes (increasing irritability, uncharacteristic impulsivity), and occasional episodes of confusion lasting minutes. She initially assumed these were stress-related. No prior seizure history. No recent head trauma.

On arrival: BP 168/94, HR 110, RR 16, SpO2 97% RA, Temp 37.0°C. Post-ictal on initial evaluation but increasingly alert. Neurological exam once fully awake: mild expressive aphasia, right-sided pronator drift, hyperreflexia right upper extremity. No papilledema on fundoscopic exam. CT head without contrast performed emergently in the ED showing a 4.1 cm heterogeneous hyperdense lesion in the left temporal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema and 5 mm midline shift. MRI brain with and without gadolinium followed, demonstrating a ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis, irregular borders, and significant surrounding FLAIR signal abnormality. No additional lesions identified. No evidence of hemorrhage within the mass.

Labs: BMP notable for glucose 194, otherwise unremarkable. CBC WNL. Coagulation studies WNL. Neurosurgery consulted in ED; patient admitted for inpatient workup and surgical planning. Levetiracetam 1000 mg IV load given in ED, then 500 mg IV BID maintenance initiated. Dexamethasone 10 mg IV given in ED, then 4 mg IV Q6H for cerebral edema. Metformin held given upcoming contrast and possible surgery. Insulin sliding scale initiated for glucose management.

Neurosurgical resection planned within 48–72 hours pending anesthesia clearance. Intraoperative MRI and awake craniotomy with cortical mapping discussed with patient given proximity to speech areas. Neuropathology will receive specimen with MGMT promoter methylation, IDH1/2, EGFR, and TERT mutation testing ordered. Patient and wife counseled about the serious nature of findings and the likely diagnosis while acknowledging that tissue confirmation is needed. Neuro-oncology, radiation oncology, and palliative care consultations placed. Goals of care discussion initiated given the clinical picture.

Patient: A.S., 43-year-old female, administrative assistant. No significant prior medical history. Non-smoker, no alcohol use. Presents with a 5-week history of worsening fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent nosebleeds. Over the past 2 weeks she has developed fever to 38.5°C, drenching night sweats, and noted petechiae on her lower extremities. She initially attributed symptoms to viral illness but became alarmed when she saw the skin findings.

Vitals: BP 104/68, HR 108, RR 18, Temp 38.3°C, SpO2 96% RA. Exam: pale conjunctivae, petechiae on bilateral lower extremities and hard palate, multiple ecchymoses on arms. Splenomegaly appreciated (~3 cm below costal margin). No lymphadenopathy. CBC: WBC 84,000/μL with 65% blasts on differential, Hgb 6.9 g/dL, Plt 18,000/μL. BMP: uric acid 9.1, LDH 1,890 U/L, creatinine 1.1. Coags: PT 16.2, PTT 48, fibrinogen 142 mg/dL, D-dimer markedly elevated — concerning for DIC. Peripheral blood smear reviewed personally: numerous large blasts with Auer rods present. Flow cytometry sent on peripheral blood. Bone marrow biopsy and aspirate performed same day with cytogenetics, FISH, and NGS panel ordered. Echo ordered given anticipated anthracycline-based therapy.

Patient admitted directly to hematology inpatient service. Initiated continuous telemetry. Transfused 2 units pRBCs and 1 apheresis unit platelets. Allopurinol 300 mg daily and IV hydration started for tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis. Cryoprecipitate administered for fibrinogen replacement. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (cefepime 2g IV Q8H) initiated given febrile neutropenia. Hematology/oncology attending at bedside. Induction chemotherapy with 7+3 regimen (cytarabine + daunorubicin) anticipated pending cytogenetics and FLT3/IDH mutational status, which may alter regimen selection. Central venous access (PICC vs. tunneled CVC) being coordinated with IR. Patient extremely anxious; social work and psychiatry consultations placed. Informed consent discussion for chemotherapy and associated risks conducted with patient and her husband.

Patient: W.H., 49-year-old female, nurse. PMH: fibrocystic breast disease, GERD. Family history significant for maternal aunt with breast cancer at age 55. G2P2, first pregnancy at 32. No prior breast biopsies. Self-referred after noticing a new right breast lump approximately 3 weeks ago. Reports the lump is firm and non-tender, does not fluctuate with her cycle. No nipple discharge, no skin changes noted by patient, no axillary lump.

Exam today: BP 118/72, HR 76, BMI 24.8. Right breast: 2.2 cm firm, irregular, non-tender mass in the right upper outer quadrant at 10 o'clock, approximately 4 cm from the nipple. Mild skin dimpling over the mass with arm elevation. No nipple inversion or discharge. One firm, mobile, approximately 1.5 cm right axillary lymph node palpable. Left breast and left axilla unremarkable. Bilateral mammogram and targeted right breast ultrasound obtained today — mammogram demonstrates a spiculated 2.4 cm mass with associated microcalcifications, BI-RADS 5 (highly suggestive of malignancy). Ultrasound confirms solid hypoechoic mass with irregular margins and an enlarged right axillary lymph node with cortical thickening. Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the breast mass and axillary node performed in-office today; specimens sent for H&E, ER/PR/HER2 IHC, and Ki-67. BRCA1/2 germline testing offered and accepted given family history; blood sent.

Ibuprofen 400 mg TID PRN for biopsy site pain. Patient asked to limit right arm activity for 24 hours. Appointment scheduled in 5 days for biopsy results review. Breast surgery and medical oncology referrals placed. MRI breast (bilateral) ordered for surgical planning. Sentinel lymph node biopsy vs. axillary dissection planning deferred pending pathology. Patient is a healthcare professional and is knowledgeable; counseled in detail about the BIRADS 5 finding, staged approach to diagnosis and management, and was provided with written materials. She is appropriately anxious and asks good questions. Genetic counseling appointment coordinated.

Patient: G.M., 72-year-old male, retired. PMH: T2DM (longstanding, recently worsening), tobacco use (50 pack-year history, currently smoking), HTN. Reports 3 months of dull mid-epigastric and back pain that radiates through to the back, worsened post-prandially, and some improvement with leaning forward. Notably, his previously controlled diabetes has become erratic over the past 2 months despite no change in medications. Wife reports he has lost significant weight — she estimates >20 lbs in the past 3 months. Over the past 3 weeks he has developed progressive jaundice, dark urine, and acholic stools. No fever, no rigors. He delayed seeking care, assuming the jaundice was liver-related from prior alcohol use.

Vitals: BP 146/88, HR 84, RR 14, Temp 36.8°C, BMI 21.1 (declining from 25.7 documented 6 months ago). Icteric sclerae, jaundiced skin. Mild RUQ and epigastric tenderness. Liver palpable 2 cm below costal margin. Non-tender, distended gallbladder palpable in RUQ (Courvoisier's sign). No ascites by percussion or ultrasound. Labs: Total bili 11.4 mg/dL, direct bili 9.2, ALT 188, AST 142, ALP 478, GGT 392. CA 19-9: 2,840 U/mL. CEA 6.1. Blood glucose 318 on presentation. BMP otherwise notable for hypokalemia (K 3.2). CBC: mild anemia. INR 1.4. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast shows a 3.5 x 2.8 cm hypoattenuating mass in the head of the pancreas with dilation of the common bile duct (1.4 cm) and pancreatic duct ("double duct sign"), no hepatic metastases, but encasement of the superior mesenteric artery >180 degrees noted. Impression from radiology: likely borderline resectable pancreatic head mass.

Gastroenterology and surgical oncology consulted emergently. ERCP with biliary stent placement planned within 24 hours for biliary decompression. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration to obtain tissue confirmation scheduled in conjunction. Insulin sliding scale initiated; metformin held. IV fluids for hydration. Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily. Ondansetron 4 mg IV Q8H PRN. Potassium repletion ordered. Surgical oncology performing multidisciplinary planning — given SMA encasement, neoadjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX vs. gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel will likely be recommended prior to surgical reassessment. Palliative care and nutrition (for TPN vs. jejunal feeds consideration) consultations placed. Family meeting scheduled tomorrow to discuss prognosis and treatment goals.

Patient: B.C., 68-year-old female. PMH: HTN, osteoporosis, CKD stage 2 (baseline Cr 1.3). Presents with a 6-month history of progressive lower back pain, rated 7/10, not relieved by NSAIDs. Reports "bone aches all over," fatigue, and 3 episodes of pneumonia in the past year (treated outpatient). No recent trauma. Denies numbness or bowel/bladder changes. Her PCP noted worsening anemia on routine labs last month and referred here.

Vitals: BP 144/88, HR 86, Temp 36.9°C, BMI 27.3. Exam: diffuse bony tenderness on palpation of thoracic and lumbar spine, no midline step-off. No organomegaly. Mild pallor. CBC: Hgb 8.4 g/dL, WBC 4.2, Plt 142,000. BMP: Cr 1.9 (worsened from baseline), Ca 11.9 mg/dL, total protein elevated. BUN 42. Serum protein electrophoresis: M-spike of 3.8 g/dL in the gamma region. Serum immunofixation: IgG kappa paraprotein. Serum free light chains: kappa 840 mg/L, lambda 12 mg/L, ratio markedly elevated. Beta-2 microglobulin 5.8 mg/L. LDH 298. 24-hr urine for Bence Jones protein ordered. Skeletal survey and MRI spine obtained: multiple lytic lesions in the skull, pelvis, and proximal femora; compression fracture at T10 and L2. Bone marrow biopsy performed today showing 65% plasma cell infiltration with karyotype and FISH for del(17p), t(4;14), t(14;16) pending.

Admitted for workup and management of hypercalcemia and renal compromise. IV normal saline hydration at 200 mL/hr.

Patient: T.N., 38-year-old female, mother of 3. Uninsured until recently, limited access to preventive care. No Pap smear in >10 years. PMH: HPV-positive noted on a Pap smear 12 years ago at another facility (records unavailable). Presents now with 4 months of post-coital bleeding, increased vaginal discharge (watery, occasionally foul-smelling), and pelvic pressure. Denies dysuria or hematuria. Has had unintentional 10-lb weight loss. No prior pelvic surgeries.

Vitals: BP 116/74, HR 90, Temp 37.2°C, BMI 22.6. On speculum exam: large, irregular, friable, exophytic cervical mass approximately 4 cm in size, bleeding easily on contact. Bimanual exam: parametrial thickening bilaterally, uterus difficult to distinguish separately from mass. No inguinal lymphadenopathy palpated. Cervical biopsy performed in clinic under local anesthesia; two specimens taken from mass. ECC deferred given obvious lesion. Urine hCG negative. CBC: Hgb 9.2 g/dL, microcytic. BMP WNL. Creatinine 0.9. HIV test obtained; result pending. CT abdomen/pelvis and MRI pelvis with contrast ordered urgently. PET-CT ordered for staging. 

Gynecologic oncology referral placed urgently; patient was seen in same-day add-on clinic by GYN-ONC attending who reviewed findings. Clinical stage at minimum IIB suspected given parametrial involvement; awaiting imaging for full assessment. Gynecologic oncology team discussed concurrent cisplatin-based chemoradiation as likely primary treatment approach. Iron supplementation and folate started for anemia. Patient counseled extensively in Spanish (interpreter used) about the findings and urgency of follow-up. Social work consulted for financial resources, transportation support. Next visit in 5 days for biopsy results and imaging review. Guardianship of children discussed per patient's expressed concern.

Patient: F.O., 58-year-old male. PMH: Hepatitis C cirrhosis (diagnosed 10 years ago, completed direct-acting antiviral therapy 3 years ago with SVR12 confirmed), prior alcohol use disorder (in remission x 5 years), T2DM. Enrolled in HCC surveillance program with 6-month ultrasound. Presenting today for follow-up after surveillance ultrasound last week noted a new 2.8 cm hepatic lesion in segment 6 with internal vascularity.

BP 118/70, HR 74, Temp 36.7°C. On exam: Spider angiomata on chest, mild palmar erythema, no asterixis. Abdomen: mildly protuberant, non-tender, splenomegaly present, no shifting dullness today. No lower extremity edema. Child-Pugh score calculated: Class B (7 points). MELD-Na 14. Labs: AFP 980 ng/mL (markedly elevated from prior 12 ng/mL 6 months ago). AST 68, ALT 52, total bili 2.1, INR 1.5, albumin 2.9, platelets 88,000, creatinine 1.0. Multiphasic CT liver with contrast performed: 2.8 cm arterially enhancing lesion with washout in the portal venous phase in segment 6 — LI-RADS 5, diagnostic for HCC per imaging criteria. No satellite lesions. Portal vein patent. No extrahepatic disease. Chest CT: no pulmonary metastases.

Patient presented to multidisciplinary liver tumor board. Given Child-Pugh B, single lesion 2.8 cm without vascular invasion, within Milan criteria — liver transplant evaluation initiated with transplant hepatology referral placed. Locoregional therapy with TACE or thermal ablation being considered as bridging therapy and discussed with interventional radiology. Sorafenib not indicated at this time given potentially curative intent. Continued abstinence from alcohol reinforced; referred back to addiction medicine for ongoing support. Rifaximin 550 mg BID and lactulose 30 mL BID continued for hepatic encephalopathy prophylaxis. Furosemide 40 mg daily and spironolactone 100 mg daily continued for portal hypertension management. Endoscopy scheduled for variceal surveillance. EBV/CMV/HIV serologies and crossmatch labs sent for transplant workup. Patient counseled regarding waitlist process and imperative for ongoing surveillance compliance.

Patient: L.W., 34-year-old female, teacher. No significant PMH. Non-smoker, no alcohol. Incidentally noted to have a thyroid nodule on CT chest obtained for workup of a pulmonary embolism 2 months ago. Asymptomatic from a thyroid standpoint — no dysphagia, no voice changes, no neck swelling noticed. No family history of thyroid cancer or MEN syndromes. No prior head/neck radiation exposure. Referred to endocrinology and presenting for further evaluation.

Vitals WNL. On neck exam: palpable left thyroid lobe nodule approximately 1.5 cm, firm, non-tender, no cervical lymphadenopathy palpated. Thyroid ultrasound obtained in clinic: 1.8 cm left thyroid nodule with irregular margins, microcalcifications, hypoechoic echotexture, taller-than-wide on transverse view — TIRADS 5. Two small left-sided level III cervical lymph nodes with abnormal echogenicity (3-4 mm). TSH 1.2 (normal). Free T4 normal. Calcitonin WNL. Calcium WNL. Fine needle aspiration biopsy of the thyroid nodule performed today under ultrasound guidance; 4 passes obtained, specimen adequate. Preliminary cytology suggests papillary thyroid carcinoma (classic variant). FNA of one cervical lymph node also performed given suspicious appearance.

Surgery referral placed for total thyroidectomy with central compartment lymph node dissection; lateral neck dissection to be determined by final cytology and intraoperative findings. Endocrinology coordinating with high-volume thyroid surgeon. Thyroxine not yet started — will await surgical planning. Patient is a young woman and is understandably anxious despite being counseled about the typically excellent prognosis of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Risks of surgery (hypoparathyroidism, recurrent laryngeal nerve injury) discussed in detail. Post-surgical radioactive iodine therapy need will depend on final pathologic staging. Thyroglobulin level ordered as baseline. Genetic testing for BRAF V600E expected on FNA specimen. Return to endocrinology 2 weeks post-op for TSH suppression initiation and RAI planning discussion.

Patient: H.P., 55-year-old male, attorney. No significant PMH. Presenting after 3 months of enlarging, painless right cervical and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Reports drenching night sweats occurring 3–4 times per week for 8 weeks, unintentional 16-lb weight loss, and intermittent fevers to 38.6°C. No throat pain, no recent infections. Reports progressive fatigue limiting his work capacity over the past month. ROS also positive for some abdominal fullness.

Vitals: BP 130/80, HR 96, Temp 38.1°C, BMI 26.2. Exam: multiple firm, matted right cervical lymph nodes (largest ~3.5 cm), right supraclavicular adenopathy (2.5 cm), non-tender. Axillary and inguinal nodes not palpable. Abdominal exam: splenomegaly ~4 cm below costal margin, mild diffuse tenderness. CBC: WBC 14,200 with left shift, Hgb 10.1 (normocytic), Plt 88,000. LDH 1,148 U/L (markedly elevated). ESR 88. Uric acid 8.4. BMP: creatinine 1.2, otherwise WNL. Beta-2 microglobulin 6.2 mg/L. HIV negative. Hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody checked (important prior to anti-CD20 therapy). Excisional biopsy of right cervical node performed by surgery today; sent for flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, cytogenetics, and FISH for MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements (to rule out double-hit/triple-hit lymphoma). Bone marrow biopsy performed in clinic. PET-CT ordered for staging. Echo ordered.

Admitted given B symptoms, cytopenias, and markedly elevated LDH. IV fluids and allopurinol for TLS prophylaxis. Acetaminophen and ibuprofen for fever and sweats symptom management (hold ibuprofen given thrombocytopenia, switched to acetaminophen only). Hematology-oncology attending at bedside; R-CHOP immunochemotherapy anticipated as first-line pending pathologic confirmation. CNS prophylaxis with intrathecal methotrexate vs. high-dose IV MTX being considered given elevated LDH and multiple sites. Anti-emetics and growth factor support will be incorporated. Patient highly engaged and wants to understand every step; provided written educational materials. Social work consulted for support needs. Follow-up with outpatient hematology-oncology scheduled post-discharge with plan to initiate cycle 1 of therapy within 5–7 days of discharge.

Patient: C.R., 62-year-old female. PMH: hypertension, nulliparous, late menopause at 56, no OCP use history. BRCA status unknown. Presenting with 2 months of progressive abdominal distension, early satiety, and vague pelvic discomfort. She initially attributed symptoms to GI issues and tried dietary modification without improvement. Over the past 3 weeks she has noted increased urinary frequency. No vaginal bleeding (postmenopausal x 6 years). No change in bowel habits. Has lost 12 lbs over 2 months.

Vitals: BP 136/82, HR 88, Temp 36.9°C. Abdomen markedly distended with shifting dullness on percussion — moderate ascites confirmed clinically and by bedside ultrasound. Bimanual pelvic exam: large, irregular, fixed right adnexal mass, approximately 8 cm by clinical estimate. Left adnexal fullness also appreciated. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: bilateral complex adnexal masses (right 9.2 cm, left 5.4 cm) with solid components and irregular septations, omental caking, peritoneal implants throughout the abdomen and pelvis, moderate-to-large ascites. No liver parenchymal lesions. CA-125: 2,240 U/mL. HE4: elevated. LDH mildly elevated. CEA and CA 19-9 ordered to evaluate for metastatic GI primary. CBC: mild anemia. BMP: creatinine 1.1, sodium 136.

Gynecologic oncology consultation placed urgently. GYN-ONC attending reviewed patient in clinic today. Paracentesis performed for symptomatic relief and cytologic diagnosis — 2.5 liters of straw-colored fluid drained. Ascites cytology sent and preliminary report shows malignant cells consistent with high-grade serous carcinoma. Tissue confirmation via core biopsy of omental implant scheduled. Germline BRCA1/2 and somatic tumor testing planned. Primary debulking surgery vs. neoadjuvant chemotherapy with interval debulking discussion underway in tumor board — given extensive peritoneal disease, neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel x 3 cycles prior to surgical assessment is preferred approach. Patient counseled about diagnosis, complexity of disease, and treatment strategy in a lengthy family meeting. Palliative care consultation placed to support symptom management and advance care planning. Ondansetron 8 mg PO TID for nausea. Furosemide 40 mg daily for ascites management. Follow-up in 5 days for biopsy results and initiation of chemotherapy planning.

Patient: J.K., 71-year-old male. PMH: BPH (on tamsulosin), HTN, T2DM. African American. PSA has been rising on annual monitoring over past 4 years (from 4.2 → 6.8 → 9.4 → 14.6 ng/mL most recently). Referred by PCP for urology consultation, presenting today for full evaluation. He denies urinary symptoms beyond pre-existing BPH symptoms (nocturia x2, weak stream). No bone pain, no hematuria, no weight loss. No family history of prostate cancer reported, though he notes his father died of unknown cancer in his 60s.

Vitals: BP 132/78, HR 72, BMI 29.1. DRE: enlarged prostate with a firm, irregular right lobe nodule. Urology arranged multiparametric MRI prostate which demonstrated a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone (1.8 cm) and a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left mid-gland. Transrectal ultrasound-guided targeted + systematic biopsy performed: 12-core systematic plus 4 targeted cores from PI-RADS 5 lesion — pathology returns Gleason 4+4

Patient: K.L., 46-year-old female. PMH: Multiple prior basal cell carcinomas, significant sun exposure history, fair-skinned, no personal or family history of melanoma. Initial primary excision of a right shoulder melanoma (Breslow 2.2 mm, Clark IV, ulcerated, no SLNB done at that time per records from outside institution 4 years ago). Lost to follow-up. Now presenting with a new raised, firm subcutaneous nodule on the right upper arm (not the scar site), new left posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and 2 weeks of severe headaches and one episode of blurry vision last week.

Vitals: BP 128/80, HR 82, Temp 36.8°C. Exam: 1.8 cm firm subcutaneous nodule right upper arm (suspected in-transit metastasis). Left posterior cervical node 2 cm, firm, non-tender. Skin survey: no additional suspicious lesions beyond prior scar site. Neurological exam: no focal deficits, no papilledema, but subjective visual changes reported by patient. LDH 520 U/L. CBC and BMP WNL. S100B and MIA ordered. Punch biopsy of subcutaneous nodule performed today in clinic; sent for H&E and BRAF V600E mutation testing by IHC and PCR. Brain MRI with contrast obtained emergently given headaches and visual symptoms: 3 intracranial lesions identified — 1.4 cm right parietal, 0.9 cm left cerebellar, 0.7 cm left frontal — all enhancing, surrounded by edema, consistent with brain metastases. PET-CT ordered for systemic staging.

Neurosurgery consulted for evaluation of brain metastases; stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) referral placed to radiation oncology for all 3 lesions given small size and good KPS. Dexamethasone 4 mg PO Q6H initiated for cerebral edema with PPI co-prescription (pantoprazole 40 mg daily). Melanoma medical oncology consulted; anticipating BRAF-targeted therapy (dabrafenib + trametinib) if BRAF V600E confirmed, or immunotherapy with nivolumab + ipilimumab if BRAF wild-type. Levetiracetam 500 mg BID started prophylactically given supratentorial lesions. Patient is a 46-year-old with young children and is very distressed; palliative care and social work consulted same day. Return in 7 days for biopsy results, staging PET-CT review, and initiation of systemic therapy planning.

Patient: P.T., 63-year-old male. PMH: HTN (on ACE inhibitor), active 30 pack-year smoker. Presenting for evaluation after an abdominal ultrasound done for an unrelated reason (gallstone workup) incidentally noted a right renal mass. Asymptomatic — no hematuria, no flank pain, no weight loss. No personal history of renal disease or prior malignancy. Family history non-contributory.

BP 148/90, HR 78, Temp 36.9°C, BMI 31.4. Abdomen soft, non-tender, no palpable renal mass. No CVA tenderness. Urinalysis: trace hematuria (2 RBCs/hpf), no proteinuria. BMP: Creatinine 1.1, GFR estimated 68. CBC WNL. LFTs WNL. CT abdomen/pelvis with and without contrast: 4.8 cm solid, heterogeneously enhancing mass in the right kidney lower pole with no extension beyond Gerota's fascia, no renal vein or IVC involvement, no regional lymphadenopathy, no adrenal involvement, no distant metastases. Radiographic appearance most consistent with RCC, clear cell type. CT chest: no pulmonary nodules or masses. Urology referral placed; appointment confirmed for next week.

Urologic oncology evaluation confirmed plan for robot-assisted partial nephrectomy given favorable tumor anatomy and imperative to preserve renal function. No biopsy recommended given planned resection. Pre-operative evaluation initiated: nuclear medicine split renal function scan ordered, cardiology clearance obtained, lisinopril held perioperatively as instructed. Surgery scheduled for 3 weeks. Patient counseled about surgical risks, recovery timeline (~4–6 weeks return to full activity), and long-term renal surveillance. Tobacco cessation strongly encouraged and patient given NRT prescription (nicotine patch 21 mg daily) plus referral to smoking cessation program. No systemic therapy needed at this time given localized disease.

Patient: N.O., 66-year-old male. PMH: Long-standing GERD (on PPI for 10 years), Barrett's esophagus diagnosed 6 years ago on endoscopy (low-grade dysplasia at that time, surveillance endoscopy lapsed). Active smoker, 1–2 alcoholic drinks nightly. BMI 33.5. Presenting with progressive dysphagia to solids over the past 3 months, now also having difficulty with soft foods. Reports odynophagia, 20-lb weight loss, and occasional regurgitation of undigested food. Denies hematemesis. Voice slightly hoarse compared to baseline per wife.

Vitals: BP 138/86, HR 90, Temp 37.1°C. Supraclavicular nodes not palpable. Mild epigastric tenderness. No hepatomegaly. CBC: Hgb 9.8, microcytic. BMP: albumin 2.6 (low), Cr 1.1. Upper GI series performed showing irregular narrowing of the distal esophagus. Upper endoscopy performed by GI: circumferential, friable, ulcerated mass extending from 32–40 cm from the incisors at the GEJ, consistent with Barrett's-related adenocarcinoma clinically. Biopsies x 6 showing well-to-moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with intestinal-type features. EUS performed at same session: T3 lesion, regional paraesophageal lymphadenopathy (N1). HER2 IHC ordered on biopsy specimen. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: no hepatic or pulmonary metastases, but paraesophageal and celiac lymph nodes enlarged. PET-CT ordered for final staging.

Thoracic surgery and medical oncology referrals placed — multidisciplinary esophageal tumor board scheduled. Neoadjuvant chemoradiation with carboplatin/paclitaxel concurrent with external beam RT (CROSS protocol) is standard of care for resectable T3N1M0 disease and will be discussed at board. Pantoprazole dose increased to 40 mg PO BID. Nutritional support urgently arranged — dietitian consultation, high-protein oral supplements TID (Ensure Plus), and percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tube placement discussed with patient for nutritional support during therapy. Ondansetron 8 mg PO TID PRN nausea. Tobacco and alcohol cessation counseled strongly with resources provided. Patient appears gaunt and frightened; social work consulted for support.

Patient: S.A., 70-year-old male. PMH: HTN, BPH. 35 pack-year smoker (current). Presenting with a 6-week history of painless gross hematuria. Reports passing clots on 3 occasions. No dysuria or urinary frequency beyond BPH baseline. No flank pain, no weight loss, no bone pain. No occupational aromatic amine exposure reported. No prior genitourinary malignancy.

Vitals: BP 142/86, HR 84, Temp 36.8°C. Abdomen soft, no suprapubic mass. Mild BPH confirmed on DRE (enlarged, smooth prostate, no nodules), PSA ordered to rule out concomitant prostate disease (result pending). CBC: Hgb 11.2 (mild anemia). BMP WNL. UA: large blood, >100 RBCs/hpf, no bacteria, no casts. Urine cytology: atypical urothelial cells present (cannot exclude high-grade urothelial carcinoma). CT urography: 2.4 cm enhancing papillary lesion on the posterior wall of the bladder, no upper tract filling defects, no hydronephrosis, no enlarged pelvic lymph nodes. No renal masses. Urology referral placed urgently; patient seen same week by urology.

Urology performed cystoscopy under general anesthesia with TURBT: a 2.5 cm sessile, papillary mass at the posterior wall biopsied and resected. Pathology: high-grade urothelial carcinoma, lamina propria invasion (T1, high-grade), no muscularis propria in specimen — re-TURBT planned in 4–6 weeks to ensure complete resection and stage accurately. Single immediate post-resection intravesical instillation of mitomycin C 40 mg administered in the OR. Urology plans intravesical BCG induction course x 6 weeks once pathologic stage confirmed on re-TURBT. Smoking cessation again strongly reinforced — patient given varenicline Rx. Hematuria has largely resolved post-procedure. Follow-up cystoscopy surveillance every 3 months x 2 years will be initiated after BCG completion. Patient counseled about recurrence risk and importance of surveillance compliance.

Patient: Y.M., 28-year-old female, graduate student. No significant PMH. Non-smoker. Presented to student health 2 weeks ago with vague left-sided abdominal pain and fullness she has noticed for approximately 6 weeks. Initially attributed to stress and dietary changes. Referred here after student health noted a palpable abdominal mass.

BP 110/68, HR 94, Temp 37.0°C, BMI 20.3. Weight 56.4 kg (down from 60 kg documented at her last visit 4 months ago — 3.6 kg unintentional loss). Abdomen: firm, non-tender 8–10 cm mass palpable in the left mid-abdomen, does not move with respiration, not pulsatile. Non-tender. Mild fullness in the LUQ. Bowel sounds present. No adenopathy palpated. No skin findings. CBC: WBC 11,800 with slight left shift, Hgb 11.6, Plt 498,000. LDH: 880 U/L (notably elevated). UA negative. BMP WNL. Uric acid 7.2. Beta-hCG negative (important given age and sex). AFP: 6 (WNL). CA-125: 28 (WNL). ESR: 78. CRP: 44. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast performed today showing a large, heterogeneous retroperitoneal mass (11.5 x 8.2 x 7.4 cm) originating from the left retroperitoneum with internal areas of necrosis and calcification, displacing but not invading adjacent bowel. Multiple retroperitoneal lymph nodes enlarged. No hepatic lesions. CT chest: no pulmonary findings. MRI abdomen ordered for better tissue characterization. PET-CT ordered. Interventional radiology consultation placed for CT-guided core needle biopsy.

The differential diagnosis is broad at this point and includes primary retroperitoneal sarcoma (liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma), lymphoma (NHL), and less likely given tumor markers, a germ cell tumor. The elevated LDH and young age raise concern for lymphoma. Full lymphoma workup including SPEP, LFTs, bone marrow biopsy (if lymphoma confirmed), and immunophenotyping of biopsy specimen will be directed by tissue results. Patient was seen alone, is clearly anxious and tearful. She called her mother during the visit. Counseled that we do not yet have a diagnosis and that the biopsy is essential before any treatment decisions. Social work consulted today. Expedited tumor board review planned once biopsy results return (estimated 5–7 days). Follow-up appointment made for 7 days to discuss biopsy results and formulate a treatment plan. Contact information provided for direct line to oncology triage nurse.

Disease: SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA — HEAD AND NECK (OROPHARYNGEAL)
Note:
Patient: O.B., 52-year-old male, non-smoker, social drinker (4–5 drinks/week). No PMH. Presenting with a 2-month history of right-sided throat discomfort and dysphagia to solids, and a progressively enlarging, painless right neck lump noted for 6 weeks. He initially attributed the throat pain to reflux. No ear pain, no voice change, no weight loss beyond 5 lbs.

Vitals: BP 124/78, HR 80, Temp 36.8°C, BMI 24.2. On exam: 3 cm firm, mobile right level II cervical lymph node. Oropharynx: right tonsillar enlargement with an irregular, somewhat indurated surface — right tonsil appears approximately twice the size of left. Neck supple. Flexible laryngoscopy performed in clinic today: right tonsillar mass extending onto the right anterior tonsillar pillar; no vocal cord involvement. No base of tongue involvement visualized. CT neck with contrast: right tonsillar mass (3.8 cm) with ipsilateral level II–III lymphadenopathy (largest node 3.2 cm). No contralateral nodes. CT chest: no mediastinal nodes or pulmonary lesions. MRI oropharynx with contrast ordered. PET-CT ordered. p16 IHC and HPV in-situ hybridization or PCR sent on anticipated biopsy specimen given non-smoking status and oropharyngeal primary — HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCC is the working diagnosis.

Panendoscopy under general anesthesia scheduled with ENT/head-neck surgery for definitive biopsy, examination under anesthesia, and tonsillectomy for diagnostic and staging purposes. Multidisciplinary head and neck tumor board referral placed. Given likely HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCC (favorable biology), primary definitive chemoradiation with cisplatin concurrent with RT vs. transoral robotic surgery (TORS) + neck dissection will be discussed based on staging. De-escalation protocols will be reviewed given expected HPV+ status. Dental evaluation ordered pre-radiation (mandatory for patients receiving head and neck RT). Baseline audiogram ordered prior to cisplatin. Swallowing evaluation (speech-language pathology) scheduled. Patient counseled about HPV-related etiology (his wife was present and both had questions about implications); they were given written resources and the ASCO patient FAQ on HPV-related cancer. Follow-up in 10 days.

Disease: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
Note: 72yo female with long-standing HTN and obesity presents with progressive DOE and 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities. Patient reports sleeping in a recliner for the last three nights due to orthopnea. On exam, BP 165/94, HR 82, SpO2 93% on RA. JVP is elevated at 10cm. S4 gallop noted on cardiac auscultation. Recent echo shows EF 55% but impaired diastolic filling and left atrial enlargement. BNP is 450 pg/mL. Started on Furosemide 40mg PO daily and Lisinopril increased to 20mg. Advised on 2g sodium restriction. Follow-up in clinic in 1 week for weight check and BMP to monitor renal function.

40yo female c/o profound fatigue, "brain fog," and 12lb weight gain over 4 months despite no change in diet. Reports cold intolerance and constipation. Vitals: Temp 97.4F, HR 58, BP 110/70. Physical exam reveals a firm, non-tender, symmetrically enlarged thyroid (Grade 1 goiter). Skin is dry and cool. TSH 14.2 mIU/L with low Free T4. TPO antibodies strongly positive. Prescribed Levothyroxine 75mcg daily to be taken on an empty stomach 30 mins before breakfast. Recheck TSH in 6 weeks to titrate dose.

55yo male presents to the ED with acute onset LLQ abdominal pain, described as cramping and constant, rated 7/10. Reports low-grade fever and nausea. Temp 100.8F, HR 105, BP 138/88. Abdominal exam shows localized tenderness and guarding in LLQ, no rebound. WBC count 16,000 with left shift. CT abdomen/pelvis reveals colonic wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding in the sigmoid colon; no abscess noted. Patient started on Ciprofloxacin 500mg BID and Metronidazole 500mg TID for 10 days. Advised clear liquid diet for 48 hours then slow advancement to low fiber. Follow-up for colonoscopy in 6-8 weeks to rule out other pathology once inflammation subsides.

31yo female presents for evaluation of intermittent paresthesia in the right arm and "electric-like" sensations running down her spine when flexing her neck (Lhermitte’s sign). Symptoms began 2 weeks ago and are slowly improving. No history of trauma. Neuro exam shows 2+ reflexes throughout, slightly diminished vibratory sense in the right hand. Cranial nerves II-XII intact. MRI brain and spine ordered with and without gadolinium to evaluate for demyelinating plaques. Prescribed Gabapentin 300mg at bedtime for sensory discomfort. Return to clinic immediately if visual changes or gait instability develop.

66yo male smoker (50 pack-year history) presents with increased cough and change in sputum color to green. RR 24, HR 110, SpO2 89% on RA. Diffuse wheezing and prolonged expiratory phase noted on auscultation. CXR shows hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms but no acute infiltrate. ABG reveals mild respiratory acidosis. Patient administered DuoNeb in clinic with moderate improvement. Prescribed Prednisone 40mg daily for 5 days and Azithromycin 500mg on day 1 followed by 250mg for 4 days. Encouraged smoking cessation and provided resources. Pulmonary function tests to be scheduled once stable.

48yo female with 6 months of symmetric morning stiffness in the PIP and MCP joints lasting over 2 hours. Reports "feeling like my hands are in tight gloves." On exam, notable boggy swelling and tenderness of the 2nd and 3rd MCPs bilaterally. Rheumatoid Factor and anti-CCP are both elevated; ESR 45, CRP 12. X-rays of hands show periarticular osteopenia but no erosions yet. Started on Methotrexate 15mg weekly and Folic Acid 1mg daily. Baseline eye exam and TB test ordered. Follow-up in 4 weeks for LFT monitoring.

22yo female c/o irregular menses (4 periods per year) and bothersome acne/hirsutism on the chin and upper lip. BMI 32. BP 122/78. Pelvic ultrasound shows "string of pearls" follicle distribution on both ovaries. Lab work reveals elevated testosterone and an LH:FSH ratio of 3:1. Fasting glucose is borderline at 105. Discussed weight loss and lifestyle modifications. Prescribed Spironolactone 50mg daily for androgenic symptoms and a combined oral contraceptive pill to regulate cycles. Referral to nutrition for metabolic management.

38yo male presents with sudden, excruciating right-sided flank pain radiating to the groin. Associated with nausea and one episode of emesis. Patient is pacing the room, unable to find a position of comfort. BP 150/95 (likely pain-related), HR 115. Urinalysis shows 3+ blood, negative nitrites. Non-contrast CT KUB reveals a 4mm stone at the UVJ. Prescribed Tamsulosin 0.4mg daily to facilitate passage and Ketorolac 10mg every 6 hours PRN for pain. Advised to strain urine and increase fluid intake to >3L/day. Return to ED for intractable pain or fever.

29yo male presents for worsening mood over the last 3 months. Reports anhedonia, early morning awakening, and significant difficulty concentrating at work. Denies suicidal ideation or intent. PHQ-9 score is 19. Physical exam and thyroid panels are unremarkable. Discussed therapy vs. medication. Patient elects for trial of Sertraline 50mg daily. Discussed "black box" warning and delayed onset of action (2-4 weeks). Follow-up in 2 weeks for a safety check and to assess tolerability.

62yo male woke up with intense pain, redness, and swelling of the left first MTP joint. Pain is so severe he cannot bear the weight of a bedsheet. Patient admits to heavy alcohol use and steak dinner last night. Exam shows an erythematous, warm, exquisitely tender toe. Serum uric acid is 8.8 mg/dL. Prescribed Indomethacin 50mg TID for 3 days then taper, along with Colchicine 0.6mg daily. Advised to avoid high-purine foods. Will consider Allopurinol in the future if episodes recur.

45yo female with chronic retrosternal burning after meals, worse when lying down. Reports occasional "sour taste" in mouth. No dysphagia or weight loss. BMI 29. Abdominal exam is benign. No occult blood in stool. Trial of Omeprazole 20mg daily for 8 weeks initiated. Advised to avoid caffeine, chocolate, and eating within 3 hours of bedtime. If no improvement in 4 weeks, will consider referral for EGD.

68yo male for routine eye exam. Patient is asymptomatic. Intraocular pressure (IOP) measured at 26 mmHg OD and 25 mmHg OS (normal 10-21). Fundoscopic exam shows increased cup-to-disc ratio (0.7) and thinning of the neuroretinal rim. Visual field testing reveals early nasal stepping. Prescribed Latanoprost 0.005% ophthalmic solution, one drop in both eyes at bedtime. Follow-up in 1 month for IOP re-check.

19yo male athlete presents after fainting during a basketball game. He reports a brief period of lightheadedness followed by loss of consciousness for approximately 30 seconds. No post-ictal confusion or tongue biting. BP 118/72, HR 55 (sinus bradycardia). 12-lead EKG shows no QT prolongation or Brugada pattern. Ordered a 48-hour Holter monitor and an echocardiogram to rule out hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Advised to refrain from competitive sports until cleared by cardiology.

52yo female with history of venous insufficiency presents with a warm, red, swollen area on her right lower leg that has spread over the last 24 hours. Well-demarcated border noted. Patient is afebrile; HR 84, BP 130/82. No fluctuance or drainage. WBC is 11,500. Prescribed Cephalexin 500mg QID for 7 days. Advised to elevate the leg and mark the borders of redness to monitor for further spread. Follow-up if she develops fevers or chills.

70yo male with urinary hesitancy, weak stream, and nocturia 4-5 times per night. AUA Symptom Score is 22 (severe). DRE reveals a smooth, firm, enlarged prostate (approx 40g) without nodules. PSA is 2.1 ng/mL (age-appropriate). Post-void residual volume is 120 mL via bladder scan. Prescribed Finasteride 5mg daily and Tamsulosin 0.4mg at bedtime. Advised to limit fluids in the evening. Re-evaluate in 3 months.

34yo female with heavy menses (menorrhagia) reports pica (craving ice) and shortness of breath when climbing stairs. Conjunctival pallor noted. Hgb is 9.2 g/dL, MCV 74 (microcytic), Ferritin 8 ng/mL. Prescribed Ferrous Sulfate 325mg daily with Vitamin C to enhance absorption. Advised on possible constipation side effects. Referral to Gynecology for management of menorrhagia. Hgb check in 4 weeks.

27yo female c/o recurrent unilateral, throbbing headaches preceded by "flashing lights" in her vision. Headaches are associated with photophobia and nausea, lasting 12-24 hours. Physical and neuro exam currently normal. Diagnosed with Migraine with Aura. Prescribed Sumatriptan 50mg at onset of aura and Topiramate 25mg daily for prophylaxis as she reports >4 episodes per month. Advised to keep a headache diary to identify triggers.

75yo male with Type 2 Diabetes and HTN for 20 years. Routine labs show Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, GFR 42 mL/min/1.73m². Urinalysis shows 2+ protein (Albuminuria). BP 142/88. Patient is currently on Metformin and Losartan. Metformin dose reduced to 500mg BID given GFR. Reinforce glycemic control (HbA1c goal <7%) and BP goal <130/80. Referred to Nephrology for co-management and renal diet education.

26yo female presents with 2 months of "aching all over," extreme fatigue, and a facial rash that appears after sun exposure. Exam shows a faint malar erythema sparing the nasolabial folds and mild swelling of the PIP joints. No oral ulcers or alopecia. Labs ordered: ANA, dsDNA, C3/C4 levels, and urinalysis. Prescribed Naproxen 500mg BID PRN for joint pain and advised strict sun protection with SPF 50+.

64yo male presents with "palpitations" and "thumping in chest" for 2 days. Denies chest pain or SOB. HR is irregularly irregular at 115 bpm. EKG confirms Atrial Fibrillation with RVR. Patient has no prior history of AFib. CHA2DS2-VASc score is 2 (HTN, Age). Prescribed Metoprolol Succinate 25mg daily for rate control and Apixaban 5mg BID for anticoagulation. Referral to Cardiology for elective cardioversion vs. rhythm control strategy.

52-year-old female with no significant past medical history presents after palpating a firm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast 6 weeks ago. Reports mild tenderness but no nipple discharge. Family history notable for mother with breast cancer at age 61. Vitals today: BP 128/76 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, RR 14/min, Temp 36.8°C, BMI 27.4 kg/m². Physical exam reveals a 2.5 cm irregular, non-mobile mass with ipsilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound confirmed a spiculated lesion; core needle biopsy positive for invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR positive, HER2 negative. MRI breast shows no contralateral disease. Staging CT negative for distant metastases; clinical stage IIB (T2N1M0). Started on anastrozole 1 mg daily pending surgical intervention. Referred to surgical oncology for lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy. Plan for adjuvant radiation and consideration of chemotherapy based on Oncotype DX score. Follow-up in 2 weeks post-surgical consult.

64-year-old male, 40 pack-year smoking history, presents with persistent cough, 10 lb unintentional weight loss over 3 months, and intermittent hemoptysis. Past history significant for COPD. Vitals: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 18/min, Temp 37.1°C, SpO₂ 92% on room air. Lung exam reveals decreased breath sounds in right upper lobe. Chest X-ray shows right upper lobe mass; CT chest demonstrates 4.8 cm spiculated lesion with mediastinal lymphadenopathy. PET scan pending. No tissue diagnosis yet; high suspicion for non-small cell lung carcinoma. Prescribed albuterol inhaler PRN and initiated nicotine patch therapy. Referred for bronchoscopy with biopsy. Plan to discuss findings at multidisciplinary tumor board. Follow-up after pathology results.

59-year-old male with history of iron deficiency anemia presents for evaluation of altered bowel habits and intermittent rectal bleeding. Colonoscopy revealed a circumferential mass in the sigmoid colon; biopsy consistent with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Vitals stable: BP 122/70 mmHg, HR 72 bpm. CT abdomen/pelvis shows regional lymph node involvement without distant metastases. CEA elevated at 8.7 ng/mL. Staged as IIIB (T3N1M0). Underwent laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with primary anastomosis. Pathology confirmed 3/18 lymph nodes positive. Started on adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy regimen. Prescribed ondansetron PRN for nausea and instructed on neutropenia precautions. Follow-up with oncology every 2 weeks during chemotherapy cycles and surveillance CEA every 3 months.

68-year-old female with new-onset diabetes and progressive epigastric pain radiating to back, 15 lb weight loss over 2 months. Vitals: BP 118/68 mmHg, HR 92 bpm, Temp 37.0°C. Physical exam reveals mild jaundice and epigastric tenderness. Labs show elevated bilirubin (3.2 mg/dL), CA 19-9 markedly elevated. CT abdomen reveals 4 cm pancreatic head mass with liver lesions consistent with metastases. Biopsy via EUS confirms adenocarcinoma. Stage IV disease. Initiated palliative chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. Prescribed oxycodone 5 mg q6h PRN for pain and pancreatic enzyme supplementation. Discussed goals of care and referred to palliative care services. Follow-up in 1 week to assess treatment tolerance.

72-year-old male with elevated PSA noted on routine screening (PSA 9.6 ng/mL). No urinary symptoms except mild hesitancy. DRE reveals firm nodule in right lobe. Vitals stable. Transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy shows Gleason 3+4=7 adenocarcinoma. MRI pelvis shows organ-confined disease without extracapsular extension. Clinical stage T2aN0M0. Discussed treatment options; patient elected for external beam radiation therapy with androgen deprivation therapy. Started on leuprolide injection. Prescribed tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly for urinary symptoms. Follow-up PSA in 3 months.

61-year-old female presenting with increasing abdominal bloating, early satiety, and pelvic discomfort. Vitals: BP 130/78 mmHg, HR 80 bpm. Exam notable for ascites. Transvaginal ultrasound shows complex adnexal mass; CA-125 elevated at 560 U/mL. CT abdomen/pelvis reveals peritoneal implants and omental caking. Underwent exploratory laparotomy with debulking surgery; pathology high-grade serous carcinoma, stage IIIC. Initiated carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. Prescribed dexamethasone pre-chemotherapy and prochlorperazine PRN nausea. Plan for 6 cycles and repeat imaging after completion. Follow-up in oncology clinic prior to each cycle.

45-year-old male with 2-week history of fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent nosebleeds. Vitals: BP 110/68 mmHg, HR 96 bpm. CBC shows WBC 35,000/µL with blasts, Hgb 8.2 g/dL, platelets 28,000/µL. Bone marrow biopsy confirms AML with FLT3 mutation. Admitted for induction chemotherapy with cytarabine and daunorubicin (7+3 regimen). Started on allopurinol for tumor lysis prophylaxis and broad-spectrum antibiotics (cefepime) for neutropenic fever risk. Plan for bone marrow reassessment on day 14. Discussed potential for stem cell transplant. Close inpatient monitoring.

38-year-old female noticed change in mole on left calf, increasing in size and irregular borders. No systemic symptoms. Vitals normal. Dermoscopy suspicious; excisional biopsy reveals superficial spreading melanoma, Breslow depth 0.8 mm, no ulceration. Sentinel lymph node biopsy negative. Stage IA. Wide local excision performed with clear margins. No adjuvant therapy indicated. Advised strict sun protection and dermatologic follow-up every 6 months.

70-year-old male with chronic gastritis presents with progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Vitals: BP 116/72 mmHg, HR 84 bpm. Endoscopy reveals ulcerated mass in distal stomach; biopsies pending. CT scan shows gastric wall thickening and enlarged regional nodes. Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL. Prescribed PPI therapy and nutritional supplementation. Referred for oncology consultation upon pathology confirmation. Follow-up in 1 week.

63-year-old male with history of hepatitis C and cirrhosis presents with right upper quadrant pain and increasing abdominal girth. Vitals: BP 108/64 mmHg, HR 90 bpm. AFP elevated at 1,200 ng/mL. MRI liver shows 3.5 cm arterial enhancing lesion with washout consistent with HCC. Child-Pugh B. No vascular invasion. Not transplant candidate due to comorbidities. Started on sorafenib. Prescribed spironolactone for ascites management. Plan for repeat imaging in 3 months.

49-year-old female with postcoital bleeding and pelvic pain. Pap smear abnormal; biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. Vitals stable. MRI pelvis shows tumor extending to parametrium but no distant metastasis, stage IIB. Initiated concurrent chemoradiation with cisplatin. Prescribed antiemetics and advised pelvic rest. Weekly labs during therapy. Follow-up after completion for response assessment.

34-year-old female with painless thyroid nodule detected on routine exam. Ultrasound shows 1.8 cm hypoechoic nodule with microcalcifications. FNA positive for papillary thyroid carcinoma. TSH normal. Underwent total thyroidectomy. Pathology confirms 1.9 cm tumor confined to thyroid, no lymphovascular invasion. Started on levothyroxine suppression therapy. Plan for radioactive iodine ablation. Follow-up thyroglobulin levels in 6 weeks.

67-year-old male with painless gross hematuria. 30 pack-year smoking history. Vitals stable. Cystoscopy reveals papillary tumor; TURBT performed. Pathology: high-grade urothelial carcinoma invading lamina propria (T1). No muscle invasion. Started intravesical BCG therapy. Prescribed phenazopyridine for dysuria. Follow-up cystoscopy in 3 months.

70-year-old female with bone pain and fatigue. Labs: calcium 11.2 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, Hgb 9.0 g/dL. SPEP shows M-spike; bone marrow biopsy reveals 40% plasma cells. Skeletal survey shows lytic lesions in vertebrae. Diagnosed with multiple myeloma, stage II. Started on bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone. Prescribed zoledronic acid monthly. Referred for evaluation for autologous stem cell transplant. Follow-up labs every cycle.

62-year-old male with progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids, 20 lb weight loss. Endoscopy reveals distal esophageal mass; biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. CT and PET show regional nodes but no distant metastases, stage III. Vitals: BP 124/78 mmHg. Started neoadjuvant chemoradiation (carboplatin/paclitaxel). Nutritional consult obtained; feeding tube placed. Follow-up imaging post-therapy to assess surgical candidacy.

58-year-old postmenopausal female with vaginal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy reveals grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma. Ultrasound shows thickened endometrium. CT negative for spread. Underwent total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Stage IA. No adjuvant therapy recommended. Follow-up pelvic exams every 6 months.

65-year-old male with incidental 4 cm renal mass found on imaging for back pain. Vitals stable. CT abdomen shows enhancing mass in right kidney without metastases. Underwent partial nephrectomy. Pathology: clear cell carcinoma, stage T1a. No adjuvant therapy required. Monitor renal function and repeat imaging in 6 months.

55-year-old female presenting with new-onset seizures and headaches. MRI brain shows 3 cm ring-enhancing lesion in right temporal lobe. Biopsy confirms glioblastoma multiforme. Vitals stable. Underwent maximal safe resection. Started on temozolomide with concurrent radiation therapy. Prescribed levetiracetam for seizure prophylaxis and dexamethasone for cerebral edema. Follow-up MRI in 2 months.

29-year-old male with painless testicular swelling. Ultrasound reveals solid mass in right testis. Tumor markers: elevated AFP and β-hCG. Underwent radical inguinal orchiectomy; pathology: nonseminomatous germ cell tumor, stage I. CT negative for metastasis. Plan for surveillance with periodic imaging and tumor markers. Discussed sperm banking prior to potential chemotherapy. Follow-up in 1 month.

73-year-old female with incidental lymphocytosis on routine labs. No B symptoms. Vitals stable. CBC shows WBC 22,000/µL with lymphocyte predominance. Flow cytometry confirms CLL. Rai stage I with mild lymphadenopathy. No treatment indicated at this time. Monitoring plan with CBC every 3 months and clinical evaluation for progression. Educated patient on infection risk and vaccination recommendations.

58F presenting with a three-week history of progressive dysphagia, initially to solids and now borderline with liquids. She reports a sensation of food "sticking" mid-sternal. No odynophagia. She has lost approximately 4kg over the past six weeks, which she attributes to eating less due to discomfort. PMH: GERD for 12 years, poorly controlled on PRN omeprazole. Social history notable for 25 pack-year smoking, quit 8 years ago. Occasional alcohol. No family history of GI malignancy. On exam, mild epigastric tenderness, no palpable lymphadenopathy, no hepatomegaly. Vitals stable: BP 128/76, HR 74, temp 36.8, weight 61kg (down from 65kg at last visit 3 months ago). Referred for urgent upper endoscopy. Barium swallow showing a smooth tapering narrowing at GEJ — radiologist flagged as likely peptic stricture but cannot exclude early Barrett's-related change or malignancy. Bloods: Hb 109 (microcytic), ferritin low at 8, otherwise unremarkable. Initiated on high-dose PPI twice daily (pantoprazole 40mg BD), iron supplementation started. Endoscopy booked within two weeks. Patient counselled that weight loss and iron-deficiency anaemia in context of prolonged GERD history requires full workup before reassurance can be given. Return immediately if dysphagia worsens or vomiting begins.

43M, referred by GP for a six-month history of vague right upper quadrant discomfort and fatigue. Describes the discomfort as a dull heaviness rather than pain, intermittent, not related to meals. Lost roughly 3kg "without trying." No jaundice noted by patient, but wife mentioned eyes looked slightly yellow on one occasion — patient uncertain. PMH: type 2 diabetes (metformin 1g BD), hyperlipidaemia (atorvastatin 40mg nocte), BMI 34. Non-drinker. No IV drug use. Born in Hong Kong, immigrated age 19. Hepatitis B surface antigen positive on today's bloods — apparently known but not followed up. AFP 38 IU/mL (mildly elevated, normal <10 in this lab). ALT 67, AST 54, bilirubin 19 (mildly elevated), albumin normal, INR normal. USS abdomen: hepatomegaly with coarse echogenic texture consistent with chronic liver disease, one ill-defined hypoechoic lesion in segment VI measuring 1.8cm — characterisation not possible on USS alone. Referred urgently to hepatology. Triple-phase CT liver ordered. Continuing metformin and atorvastatin. Hepatitis B viral load pending. Patient advised this may represent a benign lesion but AFP elevation in context of chronic hepatitis B infection with a new liver lesion cannot be managed expectantly without full characterisation.

67M with a two-month history of increasing urinary frequency, nocturia x3–4, and weak stream. He initially presented to his GP and was treated for a UTI with trimethoprim, which provided minimal improvement. PMH: benign prostatic hyperplasia (diagnosed clinically 5 years ago, on tamsulosin 0.4mg daily), hypertension (amlodipine 10mg), ex-smoker. PSA today 6.8 ng/mL — elevated but has been fluctuating between 3.2 and 5.9 over the past four years. DRE: mildly enlarged gland, smooth, no discrete nodule palpable. Urine MC&S: no growth. Creatinine and eGFR normal. USS bladder with post-void residual: 110mL residual, no hydronephrosis. Given the PSA trajectory (rising from 3.2 to 6.8 over 4 years) and persistent LUTS not responding to alpha-blocker, referred to urology for consideration of prostate biopsy. Tamsulosin dose optimised, GP to repeat PSA in 6 weeks. Patient reassured that this likely represents his known BPH but that the PSA trend cannot be dismissed without urology input.

29F presenting with a lump in her right axilla noticed three weeks ago. She is otherwise well. The lump appeared shortly after she had a mild upper respiratory tract infection. PMH: nil significant, no medications, no family history of breast cancer (she volunteered this herself, visibly anxious). On exam: a 1.8cm mobile, mildly tender lymph node in the right axilla, soft consistency, no overlying skin changes. Full breast exam: no discrete breast mass, no nipple discharge, no skin dimpling bilaterally. No other lymphadenopathy. No hepatosplenomegaly. Temp 37.2, all vitals normal.
